AI-Driven Crop Disease Prediction via MERN Stack & CNN

Agricultural ecosystems face growing pressure from fungal and bacterial pathogens that degrade crop yield, threaten food security, and increase the burden on farm management teams. Monitoring bodies and farmers must track disease reports, verify affected sites, coordinate treatments, and record farm health readings, but these tasks are often handled through manual logs and disconnected communication channels that slow response times and reduce accuracy.
This project presents a web-based Crop Disease Tracking and Monitoring System that digitalizes and centralizes the entire workflow. Farmers can submit disease incidents, administrators can verify affected locations, and the integrated CNN model compares uploaded image readings against predefined disease thresholds to detect hazardous conditions early. Once treatment is verified, a digital agricultural report is generated and made available through a central dashboard, improving responsiveness, transparency, and decision-making in farm management.
Digital tracking can reduce reporting delays, improve verification accuracy, and enable faster treatment decisions for affected crops.
Manual reporting risks delay & poor tracking

Crop diseases are an escalating threat to global agriculture. Agricultural teams must track incoming disease reports from many sources, verify affected crops, assign experts, and record field data, typically relying on manual logs, scattered spreadsheets, and disconnected communication.
This creates delays in identifying outbreaks, makes it harder to coordinate treatments across teams, and increases the risk of incomplete or inconsistent farm records. Farmers and field officers need a centralized digital system that can manage the full lifecycle of a disease report, from submission and verification to treatment coordination and compliance tracking, with clear role-based access for farmers, field officers, and administrators.
